name: Ludwig van Beethoven
hook: The deaf genius behind nine symphonies and the first name in every classical-music category.

facts.label: Bonn to Vienna
facts.statement: Beethoven was born in Bonn in 1770 and moved to Vienna in 1792; he died there in 1827 and was buried in the city.

facts.label: Fidelio
facts.statement: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera, and it had little early success — Vienna was occupied by French troops when it premiered.

facts.label: Symphony No. 9
facts.statement: The Ninth Symphony, completed in 1824, ends with a choral setting of Schiller's "Ode to Joy," later adopted as the European Union's anthem.

facts.label: Eroica
facts.statement: The Third Symphony, "Eroica," was inspired by Napoleon; disillusioned with him, Beethoven changed its title from "Bonaparte."

facts.label: Symphony No. 5
facts.statement: The Fifth Symphony, with its famous four-note opening, was the first of his symphonies to use the piccolo and trombone.

facts.label: Moonlight Sonata
facts.statement: The Piano Sonata No. 14 in C-sharp minor is known as the "Moonlight Sonata," a nickname from a poet's image of a boat on Lake Lucerne at night.

facts.label: Für Elise
facts.statement: The bagatelle "Für Elise" is Bagatelle No. 25 in A minor, and nobody knows for sure who the title girl was.
